record.original_question: Can one solve enumeration problems for restricted classes of parking functions on rooted trees or on mappings, rather than only for the unrestricted parking functions considered in the existing counting results?

evidence.quote: (6) One could consider enumeration problems for some restricted parking functions for trees (or mappings).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let T be a rooted tree on the vertex set {1,2,...,n} with a distinguished root. A parking function on T is a sequence (a_1, a_2, ..., a_n) of vertices of T (the preferences of n drivers) such that the following parking process succeeds: drivers arrive in order; driver i starts at vertex a_i and proceeds along the unique directed path from a_i toward the root, parking at the first unoccupied vertex encountered; the sequence is a parking function on T if every driver successfully parks. The same definition extends to parking functions on a mapping (functional digraph) f:[n]→[n], where each driver follows the iterated images of f until reaching an unoccupied vertex.

A "restricted" class of parking functions is a subfamily defined by combinatorial conditions on the preference sequence (a_1, ..., a_n) and/or on the underlying tree or mapping; examples of natural restrictions include: prime parking functions; parking functions with prescribed displacement statistics; parking functions whose preferences avoid given patterns; parking functions in which prescribed drivers must park at prescribed vertices; parking functions on trees of a fixed combinatorial family (ordered, unordered, binary, plane, etc.); and parking functions on mappings with constraints on cycle lengths or component sizes.

Problem. Develop exact and asymptotic enumeration formulas (for instance, closed-form counts, generating-function characterizations, or asymptotic equivalents as n→∞) for natural restricted classes of parking functions on rooted trees and on mappings, generalizing the known counting results that are available for the unrestricted case.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works address restricted parking functions on rooted trees and mappings, including prime parking functions on rooted trees (Király–Tóthmérész/Lackner–Panholzer style results), parking function varieties for combinatorial tree models, tree parking distributions, and 2025 work on records of trees and parking functions. These resolve specific restricted enumeration problems but do not exhaust the broad program; the general problem of enumerating arbitrary restricted classes of tree/mapping parking functions remains an active research direction with many open cases.

status_evidence.claim: Restricted (prime) parking functions on rooted trees have been enumerated for several tree families.

status_evidence.title: Parking function varieties for combinatorial tree models
status_evidence.snippet: Studies parking-function-type objects associated to combinatorial tree models.
status_evidence.claim: Restricted variants on tree models are being actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry in Tree Parking Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) study of tree parking distributions with structural restrictions.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2025 progress on restricted tree parking enumeration.

status_evidence.title: On weary drivers, records of trees, and parking functions
status_evidence.snippet: Connects records of trees with parking function enumeration.
status_evidence.claim: Further restricted enumeration results obtained in 2025.
